OpenElixir-02 2.0.0, a personal build based on OpenElixir-02 1.4: **swing with a steady clock**,
**faster rolls**, a **working Euclidean generator** and a set of stock firmware fixes.

> Not official Erica Synths firmware, not affiliated with or approved by Erica Synths, and not an
> upstream OpenElixir-02 release. Install it at your own risk.

## Breaking change: the clock outputs no longer swing by default

The MIDI clock out and the clock outputs used to swing with the shuffle (the clock itself was
stretched). Now they stay straight. If you synced other gear to the LXR and relied on it swinging
along, set config "swg" (2nd page) to `Clk`.

## Swing with a steady clock

- Swing doesn't stretch the clock any more. The 2nd and 4th 16th of each beat are scheduled late,
  exactly where they were before (every swing value), and sound in the first audio block at or after
  that time.
- MIDI clock out and clock outputs are steady at any swing (before: 5.8-50.7 ms between MIDI clocks
  at swing 64 and 150 bpm instead of 16.7 ms).
- Flams and arps on swung steps keep their spacing (they were squeezed). A swung step moves as a
  whole; a newer step's note cuts the older steps' remaining repeats, a step's own note always plays
  (also when micro-shifted late).
- Following an external clock (MIDI or analog), steps start on the clock: no more dropped notes with
  swing, and notes no longer come one tick (about 5 ms at 120 bpm) late.
- Live recording snaps to the swung grid, and hits played slightly early no longer land one step too
  early (also without swing).
- Config "swg": `Not` (default) = clock outputs straight, `Clk` = they swing like the notes, spread
  evenly over the rest of a swung step. Saved with the settings; older settings files get `Not` (a
  1.4 settings file keeps its "lim" setting, which the loader used to reset).

## Faster rolls

- Speeds, slowest to fastest: One, 1/1, 1/2, 1/4, 1/8, 8T, 16, 16T, 32, 32T, 64 (T = triplet).
- Locked to the pattern's grid on tracks of any length (a 1/4 roll on a 15-step track had an uneven
  gap at every wrap).
- 16 and slower swing with their step; 8T, 16T, 32, 32T and 64 stay even.
- Pressed mid-step, the first hit comes within one roll interval; released, no more hits.

## Modal voice engine (from upstream OpenElixir-02, unreleased there)

- A fifth engine for any voice slot (SHIFT + KIT): up to 24 tuned resonators struck by a mallet,
  a noise burst or a bow. Structure blends string, bar, membrane and bell mode patterns; damping,
  brightness, strike position, hardness and the number of partials (8-24) shape it. Bells, bars,
  gongs, tuned metal and percussion, played with the step notes.
- Kits using it load with the slot's stock engine on older OpenElixir versions and the stock
  firmware.
- Clicking the encoder on a parameter shows the full name of its value (also from upstream).

## Analog voice engine: 808, 909 and acoustic instruments

- A sixth engine for any voice slot (SHIFT + KIT), from AnalogModels by G3nzalo: 38 instruments
  modelled after the circuits of the TR-808 (kick, snare, toms, congas, rim shot, claves, clap,
  maracas, cowbell, hi-hat, cymbal) and TR-909 (kick, snare, toms, rim shot, clap, hi-hat, crash,
  ride), and gamelan, djembe, conga and taiko instruments. Not samples: each is synthesized like the
  original circuit or instrument works. Sounds exactly as in AnalogModels.
- `ins` picks the instrument, `sat` is a tube saturator; decay sets the length, coarse 0 is the
  original tuning, velocity is the accent. Choosing an instrument sets the voice up to play like the
  original. Lock `ins` on a step for another instrument on that step.
- Kits using it load with the slot's stock engine on older OpenElixir versions and the stock firmware.
- Its first page shows `coa fin ins sat`; the Mod page shows the velocity settings first, and the FM
  page says "analog voice has no FM".
- Fix: a received NRPN 98 for the modal (and analog) engine switched the sound but not the menu.

## Fixes

- Playing a swung 16th live with a roll button (speed 16 or slower): a press after the step's
  straight start but before its swung hit lost that hit, so tapping the swung 16ths played and
  recorded nothing. A hit now counts by its swung time. (Found on the hardware.)
- A new project (loading a project slot that was never saved) showed 120 bpm but played on at the
  previous project's tempo, with its other settings too, until the value was touched. Stock firmware bug.
- Switching a voice's engine no longer drops audio. It scanned the step locks of all 64 patterns in
  one go, holding up the audio for about 8 ms (dropouts on every switch at a high load); now the
  audio keeps playing during the scan and while the voice's settings are sent.
- Menu: on an engine without some of the template's settings, a first screen without settings
  shows the second one, a page without any says so, and the encoder no longer edits an empty place.
- Euclidean generator: the hits are spread again (16 steps with 2 hits played steps 1 and 2 instead
  of 1 and 9). The generator relied on undefined behaviour that GCC 15 compiled away.
- Oscillators below 440 Hz: the same undefined behaviour chose their wavetable; now explicit, with
  the same result as before (the sound doesn't change).
- From the 1.4.1 build: MIDI bank select (CC 0) no longer writes past an array; shuffled tempo
  without integer rounding; morphing and kit loads no longer send MIDI transport slots as sound
  parameters (clicks, changed Drum 1 drive); copy mode clears all voice LEDs; modulation reads no
  NULL pointer; no debug sample at boot; Euclid 16-step tracks get length 16 (not 0); a freshly
  formatted card gets a valid project 0; selecting a pattern no longer reads past the Euclid
  settings.

## Under the hood

- One timing path: a queue of hits per track with exact times replaces the stock flam/shift
  playback and its shared choke flags (review S-B4). ITCM about the same as 1.4.
- Tests (host): the Analog instruments bit-identical to AnalogModels' source, the Analog voice
  checked against the instruments' definitions (decay, pitch, accent, retrigger, setup, step locks),
  Modal and Analog regression renders, menu page layout and reachability, engine switching (step
  locks, audio yields), sequencer timing harness with an independent check of the timing rules (56
  scenarios, also jittered and ramped external clock, stop and start mid-bar, recording at the
  middle between steps), settings defaults, Euclidean generator (with the UB sanitizer), engine and
  parser tests. A build check refuses to make an update image that could touch the bootloader.

## Installing

1. Copy `LXR_OpenElixir-02_V2.0.0.img` to the top folder of the SD card and delete any other
   `LXR*.img` files there.
2. Switch the LXR-02 off, insert the card, hold the encoder button and switch it on. Keep holding
   until "LXR Updater" appears.
3. Wait for "Update OK! Please Reboot!", then switch the LXR off and on again (without holding the
   encoder).

To go back, install the previous image the same way. Kits, patterns and settings stay compatible.
